descriptor.scene: NOBODY IS IN THIS PICTURE: no hands, no figures, no faces. The dial face itself is the subject, LARGE, seen straight on and filling most of the frame: the one great circular dial on the engine's cream top, its single bold ink needle standing exactly UPRIGHT at mid-dial. At the dial's LEFT end, the small snail mark; at its RIGHT end, the small winged-block mark; nothing else on the face, no numbers, no tick marks, no lettering. The light is warm and even, the cream of the dial glowing softly, a calm sliver of the engine's rounded body visible around the dial's edge. Quiet, certain, balanced. The lower right of the frame stays a calm field of soft cream.
negatives: any hand, finger or figure in frame
numbers, tick marks, scale markings or lettering on the dial
the needle leaning left or right (it stands exactly upright)
descriptor._caption: Too hot burns the trust down. Too cold never builds it. Somewhere between the roar and the silence there is a third setting. The old story had it right: you are looking for just right.

No whole figures and no faces are in shot, because the camera is too close for them, NOT because anybody left the room. the-pace-engine exactly as its reference plate: The identical machine every founder receives on the far side of the portal: a waist-high rounded machine body in flat cream, resting on a low base, with ONE large circular dial on its top and nothing else. The dial carries a single bold needle. At the dial's left end sits a small snail mark; at the dial's right end sits a small winged-block mark (the deck's dial glyphs, a cross-artifact echo of takeoffwithclaude.com's Goldilocks-pace slide). The engine can run at any speed; the dial is the only control it has. The machine itself never differs between founders and never changes between states: only the needle's position, the glow, and what the engine is putting out change. Proportions are pinned as numbers and shared by every state. The machine stands waist-high to an adult figure: body 0.95 m tall on a 0.10 m base (about 1.05 m overall against a 1.7 m adult). The body is 1.0 m wide; the dial's diameter is 0.5 m, roughly HALF the body width, standing upright and centered on the top of the body, its face toward the viewer so it reads like a gauge (locked in the blessed master, 2026-08-09). The needle pivots from the dial's center: upright at mid-dial in the steady state, hard right in roar, hard left in cold. The snail mark sits at the left end of the dial's arc, the winged-block mark at the right end; each glyph is small, about one-eighth of the dial's diameter. In frame the engine sits on the ground plane, whole and unobstructed enough that the dial and both glyphs stay legible. Ink outlines with flat cream fills (warm cream body, slightly deeper cream base), terracotta-compatible accents; the needle and the two dial glyphs are drawn in ink. State-dependent only: steady adds calm, even warm hum lines rising gently off the body; roar adds a hot glow around the engine and motion blur in its output; cold shows the engine dark and untouched, its cream dimmed toward dusk with NO glow and no hum lines. Never neon, never HUD chrome, never glossy plastic, never 3D render sheen. Waist-high to an adult: the top of the machine body reaches an adult's waist, and the dial on top sits about hip-to-navel height. In a wide shot it reads as a generous household-appliance-sized machine a founder stands beside, never a room-sized turbine and never a handheld gadget. THERE ARE NO PEOPLE AND NO CHARACTERS OF ANY KIND IN THIS IMAGE. No person, no figure, no head, no shoulder, no arm, no hand, no silhouette, no reflection of a person, and nobody seated in any chair. Any place a figure might be expected is empty. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, any hand, finger or figure in frame, numbers, tick marks, scale markings or lettering on the dial, the needle leaning left or right (it stands exactly upright), a second dial or gauge. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
